focus: Live capture surface and runtime matrix (gaps 2, 3, 4, 7, 8 mechanism)
noveltyJustification: 8 of 10 findings were new mechanisms or paths; 2 (the gap existence and the Codex policy claim) were partially new because the charter named the gap but not its location.
keyQuestions: Which of the eight known gaps are worth closing, and what is the smallest change that closes each one?
What does each runtime actually expose for live capture, and are the Cursor "unverified" and Hermes "absent" rows worth filling or deleting?
ruledOut: Treating gap 3 as a missing Codex adapter
Counting gate/pause hooks as capture adapters

label: The live capture surface is four producers, not five: Claude PostToolUse, Devin PostToolUse, Pi tool_result extension and the OpenCode tool.execute.after plugin; no Cursor or Hermes adapter folder exists.
All four producers funnel into one queue core owning identity, filtering, locking, dedup and the nudge cursor; per-runtime code is payload mapping only, so nudge parity is cheap.

The pending-answer nudge exists on two of six runtimes: Claude Stop hook and OpenCode experimental.chat.system.transform; Devin and Pi capture but never nudge, Codex has no live producer, Cursor/Hermes have no adapter.
Gap 7 is a consumer problem: the Claude nudge is written as a bare systemMessage to stdout after the Stop hook resolves, so at a real session exit no reader consumes it.
The nudge cursor is session-scoped on disk, so a next-session reader cannot see a prior session's pending count; any session-start fix needs a bounded queue scan or a project-level pending marker.

The coverage matrix has six runtime columns and no Hermes column; the Cursor cell records "unverified: no answered question tool call was found to probe", an absence of evidence kept as a permanent state.

coverage-rationale.md carries no decision-capture section, so the Codex "by-design" and Cursor "unverified" cells are the only matrix cells with no recorded justification, contrary to the README's own pointer.

Gap 3 is a tooling-policy constraint, not an information constraint: the Codex rollout sweep reads the same answered tool calls a live hook would see, so the cell describes the read location, not missing data.
Gap 8 is a two-shape main() split: transcript, opencode and devin sweeps return 1 with an error row, while codex and pi return null on an unreadable transcript and exit 0 with no output.
Pi already imports recoveredRecords from its own sweep so live and swept records share one mapping, while the OpenCode plugin re-implements that mapping locally in answerMap.

direction: Treating gap 3 as a missing Codex live adapter
reason: The rollout already carries the answers; a live read would need per-user hook trust or duplicate the rollout parse inside the runtime, so the sweep is the correct shape.

direction: Counting gate and pause hooks as capture adapters
reason: They share the hooks tree but write no decision-capture queue rows.
